races.title: State Assembly, District 76
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Darshana Patel
cands.bio: Democrat and research scientist with a Ph.D. in biophysics, formerly in oncology research at Genentech. Poway Unified school board trustee 2016–2024, including time as board president. Elected to the California Assembly (District 76) in 2024, taking office December 2024. Also served on the state API Affairs commission.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.
Her 2026 survey also lists Peace Officers Research Association of California, California Professional Firefighters, Gun Sense Voter, Planned Parenthood and CA YIMBY among her endorsers.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm where she was raised. Her high school is listed as Apple Valley High School, but the page does not say which state, and we found no year she moved to California. We found no documented stances on data centers or development, and no records of deeds such as bills signed or actions taken in office that match the platform topics. Her Ballotpedia page lists sponsored bills only in a table that did not load, so her claims about authoring AB 1834, AB 1959 and other bills come from her own survey and were not checked against legislative records. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had. The 2016 survey page was cut off, so her views on charters and other school issues from that year are incomplete.

local.label: Roots 55: She was born in Pittsburgh. The record shows her in California as an adult since at least her 1996 Occidental College degree, followed by UC Irvine (Ph.D. 2002) and UC Berkeley (2009), and in the Rancho Peñasquitos area for about 13 years as of 2024. Where she grew up is not clearly established.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Research scientist (biotechnology and oncology research), Poway Unified school board trustee 2016–2024 including board president, and member of the California State Assembly since December 2024.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the Assembly plus eight years of elected local office overseeing a district budget and policy, which fits the high band. Committee seats and advisory boards were not counted, and her career before politics was in science, not law or budgeting.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: In her 2026 Ballotpedia survey she said she has fought property tax increases that would price neighbors out of their homes.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2026 survey she said she wrote AB 1959 and a bill closing a loophole on threats of mass violence, as part of making public safety her top responsibility. This is her own description of her bills.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2024 survey she listed protecting women's reproductive rights among her priorities.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In a 2016 school board candidate survey she ranked expanding school choice options last of seven issues for the board.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Carrie S. Espinoza Villanueva
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 76. Works at Palomar College in the Trades Departments. Says she previously owned and managed small businesses in manufacturing, diesel remanufacturing, home rehabilitation and ranch operations. Has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists a Reform California endorsement, along with voter-guide recommendations from The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, Conservative California, Based in Malibu, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she came to California. No record of prior elected office or legislative work turned up. We found no documented actions in office, since she has not held one. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or growth limits, property tax relief for homeowners, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her business history and Palomar College job come only from her own campaign site, with no independent reporting found. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so her own answers there are unavailable.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Works at Palomar College supporting trades programs (welding, auto, diesel, HVAC, water technology, zero-emissions vehicle technology).
